subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Neither the teacher nor the students ___ in the hall.
explanation: With neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject is "students", which is plural, so the verb is "are".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The principal, as well as the teachers, ___ attending the meeting.
explanation: "As well as the teachers" is only additional information. The real subject is "the principal", which is singular, so the verb is "is".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

She has been living in Ibadan ___ 2015.
explanation: "Since" is used with a point in time (2015). "For" is used with a length of time, as in "for ten years".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

You will come tomorrow, ___?
explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag, and the tag repeats the auxiliary verb. "You will" gives "won't you".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
explanation: In an unreal or imagined condition, "were" is used for all persons: "If I were you".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

He prefers reading ___ watching television.
explanation: "Prefer" is followed by "to", not "than": prefer one thing to another.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The man ___ car was stolen has reported to the police.
explanation: "Whose" shows possession: the car belongs to the man.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

One of the boys ___ absent yesterday.
explanation: The subject is "one", not "boys", so the verb is singular. "Yesterday" requires the past tense: "was".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I look forward to ___ from you.
explanation: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by the -ing form: "hearing".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

By this time next year, I ___ my degree.
explanation: The future perfect ("will have completed") is used for an action that will be finished before a stated time in the future.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.

The manager was RELUCTANT to approve the request.
explanation: "Reluctant" means not willing to do something. "Unwilling" is nearest in meaning.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.

The lawyer gave a LUCID explanation of the case.
explanation: "Lucid" means easy to understand. "Clear" is nearest in meaning.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.

It was an ARDUOUS journey across the desert.
explanation: "Arduous" means needing great effort; very hard. "Difficult" is nearest in meaning.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.

The new policy will ALLEVIATE the suffering of the poor.
explanation: To alleviate is to make something less severe. "Ease" is nearest in meaning.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals.

The chief was known for his GENEROSITY.
explanation: Generosity is willingness to give freely. Its opposite is stinginess, an unwillingness to give or spend.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals.

The witness gave a VAGUE account of the accident.
explanation: "Vague" means not clear or definite. Its opposite is "precise". Note that "unclear" is a synonym, not the opposite.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals.

The secretary is always PUNCTUAL.
explanation: "Punctual" means arriving at the right time. Its opposite is "late".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best explains the expression.

Bola let the cat out of the bag.
explanation: "To let the cat out of the bag" is an idiom meaning to reveal a secret, usually by mistake.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best explains the expression.

The quarrel between the two neighbours was a storm in a teacup.
optionC: It was a great fuss about a small matter.
explanation: "A storm in a teacup" means a lot of fuss or anger about something unimportant.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best explains the expression.

After years of rivalry, the two families decided to bury the hatchet.
explanation: "To bury the hatchet" means to end a quarrel and become friendly again.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best explains the expression.

Emeka is the black sheep of the family.
optionA: He is the darkest in complexion.
optionD: He brings disgrace to the family.
explanation: "The black sheep of the family" is a member who is regarded as a disgrace or an embarrassment to the rest.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best explains the expression.

After his suspension, Tunde promised to turn over a new leaf.
optionB: to change his behaviour for the better
explanation: "To turn over a new leaf" means to start behaving in a better way.

subject: ENG
text: Which of the following best expresses the meaning of the proverb "A stitch in time saves nine"?
optionB: Nine people work better than one.
optionC: Dealing with a problem early prevents a bigger one.
optionD: Time should never be wasted on small things.
explanation: The proverb teaches that acting on a small problem at once saves much more work later.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The judge granted bail to the ___.
explanation: In the register of law, a person charged with an offence in court is "the accused".

subject: ENG
text: Which of the following words belongs to the register of medicine?
explanation: A diagnosis is a doctor's identification of an illness. "Verdict" belongs to law, "dividend" to finance and "sermon" to religion.

subject: ENG
text: The words "shares", "dividend" and "broker" belong to the register of
explanation: Shares are bought and sold through brokers on the stock exchange, and a dividend is the profit paid to shareholders.

subject: ENG
text: A formal letter that begins with "Dear Sir" should end with
explanation: When a formal letter opens with "Dear Sir" or "Dear Madam", it closes with "Yours faithfully". "Yours sincerely" is used when the person is addressed by name.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the most appropriate option for a formal notice.

The meeting has been ___ till next week.
explanation: "Postponed" is the formal word. "Put off" has the same meaning but is informal, and "pushed" and "shifted" are not standard in this sense.

subject: ENG
text:
Identify the figure of speech in the sentence.

The wind whispered through the trees.
explanation: Whispering is a human action. Giving a human quality to the wind is personification.

subject: ENG
text:
Identify the figure of speech in the sentence.

He is as brave as a lion.
explanation: A comparison made with "as" or "like" is a simile.

subject: ENG
text:
Identify the figure of speech in the sentence.

The classroom was a zoo.
explanation: The classroom is said to be a zoo directly, without "like" or "as". That is a metaphor.

subject: ENG
text:
Identify the figure of speech in the sentence.

I have told you a million times to close the door.
explanation: "A million times" is a deliberate exaggeration for emphasis, which is hyperbole.

subject: ENG
text:
Identify the figure of speech in the sentence.

Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.
explanation: The consonant sound /p/ is repeated at the beginning of nearby words. That is alliteration.

subject: ENG
text:
Identify the figure of speech in the sentence.

The child is the father of the man.
explanation: The statement seems to contradict itself, yet it contains a truth: the character formed in childhood shapes the adult. That is a paradox.

subject: ENG
text: "The old man passed away last night." The expression "passed away" is an example of
explanation: "Passed away" is a mild way of saying "died". A mild expression used in place of a harsh one is a euphemism.

subject: ENG
text: "Although it rained heavily, the match continued." This is a
explanation: It has one main clause ("the match continued") and one subordinate clause ("Although it rained heavily"), which makes it a complex sentence.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the passive form of the sentence.

The boy kicked the ball.
optionA: The ball is kicked by the boy.
optionB: The ball was kicked by the boy.
optionC: The ball has been kicked by the boy.
optionD: The boy was kicked by the ball.
explanation: The object "the ball" becomes the subject, and the tense stays the same. "Kicked" is simple past, so the passive is "was kicked".

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the correct reported form of the sentence.

She said, "I am tired."
optionA: She said that I am tired.
optionB: She said that she is tired.
optionC: She said that I was tired.
optionD: She said that she was tired.
explanation: After a reporting verb in the past, the tense moves back (am → was) and the pronoun changes to fit the speaker (I → she).

subject: ENG
text: Which of the following sentences is correctly constructed?
optionA: Walking down the road, I saw a tree fall.
optionB: Walking down the road, a tree fell.
optionC: Walking down the road, the tree was seen.
optionD: Walking down the road, there was a tree.
explanation: The phrase "Walking down the road" must describe the subject that follows it. Only in the first sentence is the subject ("I") the one doing the walking. The others have a dangling modifier.

subject: ENG
text: In the sentence shown in the diagram, which numbered part is the object?
explanation: The object receives the action of the verb. Ask "passed what?" The answer is "the examination", which is part 3.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the letters in brackets.

b(ea)t
explanation: "Beat" has the long vowel /iː/. "Key" is pronounced /kiː/, with the same vowel. "Bit" has /ɪ/, "bet" has /e/ and "bait" has the diphthong /eɪ/.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the letter in brackets.

c(u)p
explanation: "Cup" has the vowel /ʌ/. "Son" is pronounced /sʌn/. "Put" has /ʊ/, "cot" has /ɒ/ and "cart" has /ɑː/.

subject: ENG
text:
Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the letters in brackets.

(ch)emist
explanation: In "chemist" the letters "ch" are pronounced /k/, as in "school". In "church" they are /tʃ/, and in "chef" and "machine" they are /ʃ/.

subject: ENG
text: Choose the word that rhymes with "though".
explanation: "Though" is pronounced /ðəʊ/ and "sew" is /səʊ/, so they rhyme. "Tough" ends in /ʌf/, "cough" in /ɒf/ and "through" in /uː/.

subject: ENG
text: Which of the following words is stressed on the second syllable?
explanation: "Begin" is stressed on the second syllable: be-GIN. The others are stressed on the first: TA-ble, HAP-py, WA-ter.

subject: ENG
text:
The word in capitals carries the emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the answer.

JOHN bought the car.
explanation: The stress on JOHN shows that the person is being corrected. The matching question names a different person: "Did Peter buy the car?"

subject: ENG
text: The diagram shows the stress pattern of a two-syllable word. Which of the following words has this pattern?
explanation: The big dot comes first, so the first syllable is stressed. "Student" is STU-dent. "Remain", "about" and "below" are all stressed on the second syllable.

subject: ENG
text:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows.

"For years the people of Oke-Ado fetched water from a stream three kilometres away. Children missed school to carry it, and many fell ill after drinking it. When the borehole was finally sunk in the market square, attendance at the village school rose within a term, and the clinic recorded far fewer cases of typhoid. The elders, who had once doubted the project, now guard the borehole jealously."

According to the passage, one effect of the borehole was that
explanation: The passage states that "attendance at the village school rose within a term" after the borehole was sunk. The other options are not supported by the passage.

subject: ENG
text:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows.

"For years the people of Oke-Ado fetched water from a stream three kilometres away. Children missed school to carry it, and many fell ill after drinking it. When the borehole was finally sunk in the market square, attendance at the village school rose within a term, and the clinic recorded far fewer cases of typhoid. The elders, who had once doubted the project, now guard the borehole jealously."

The word "jealously", as used in the passage, means
explanation: To guard something jealously is to protect it very carefully. In this context the word has nothing to do with envy.

subject: ENG
text:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows.

"For years the people of Oke-Ado fetched water from a stream three kilometres away. Children missed school to carry it, and many fell ill after drinking it. When the borehole was finally sunk in the market square, attendance at the village school rose within a term, and the clinic recorded far fewer cases of typhoid. The elders, who had once doubted the project, now guard the borehole jealously."

Which of the following best summarises the passage in one sentence?
optionA: The borehole improved school attendance and health in Oke-Ado and won over the elders.
optionB: The people of Oke-Ado used to fetch water from a stream three kilometres away.
optionC: Typhoid is caused by drinking dirty water from streams.
optionD: The elders of Oke-Ado guard the borehole in the market square.
explanation: A summary gives the main points without detail: the borehole's benefits and the elders' change of mind. The second and fourth options cover only one detail each, and the third states something the passage does not say.
